summary: Georgia's tower list says this Emanuel County tower was moved from Oak Park; a 2007 article already calls it decommissioned at the lodge.

facts.status_note: Called decommissioned in a March 2007 article; no source confirms it stands at the lodge today.

access.note: No source describes access to the tower. The lodge sells pheasant shoots as packages, which does not show whether the old tower is open to the public.

events.note: The list says the tower was moved from Oak Park, with no date. The year shown is the earliest date a source places the tower at the lodge (a March 2007 article). The move happened by then; its exact date is unknown.

evidence.supports: List entry for the lodge site says the tower was moved from Oak Park
evidence.quote: flat creek lodge, 32.66519,-82.25524 ,Emanuel,289,moved from oak park

evidence.supports: List keeps a separate Oak Park Lookout Tower entry in Emanuel County, tagged gfc-111
March 2007 article lists a decommissioned fire tower from Oak Park among the lodge's features
evidence.quote: a decommissioned fire tower from Oak Park in Emanuel County

evidence.supports: Lodge sits in a 2,000-acre pine forest about nine miles from downtown Swainsboro
evidence.quote: 2,000-acre pine forest located about nine miles from downtown Swainsboro

evidence.supports: Article describes the lodge as a five-year-old facility
Lodge described as a hunting and fishing complex
evidence.quote: a hunting and fishing complex complete with spa
Every package includes a lodge meal, birds cleaned and packaged to take home

evidence.supports: Pheasant shoot structure is a concealed central tower from which birds are released
evidence.quote: Birds are released from our concealed central tower

notes_for_editor: The move from Oak Park rests on the list and one 2007 magazine article; neither gives a move date. The list still carries a separate Oak Park entry (GA042, 32.37740,-82.32124, gfc-111), so the two records may describe one tower or the Oak Park entry may be stale; check before merging. The lodge's pheasant tower is a shooting structure; no source links it to the fire tower, so the story does not. Elevation 289 is read as feet from the brief's 88.1 m; the list does not state units. Access is not sourced for the tower; the story says so and does not call the tower private.
